originalAlarm.description: Branch condition evaluates to a garbage value

sanitizedDescription: Branch condition evaluates to a garbage value
presenceCondition:
(or (and CONFIG_SLOB (not CONFIG_FORCE_MAX_ZONEORDER) CONFIG_SLOB)
    (and (not CONFIG_SLOB) (not CONFIG_FORCE_MAX_ZONEORDER) (not CONFIG_SLOB)))
model:
(define-fun CONFIG_SLOB () Bool
  true)
(define-fun CONFIG_FORCE_MAX_ZONEORDER () Bool
  false)
reasoning: TRUE POSITIVE (UNDER-CONSTRAINED): 0f8f8094d28.c (Linux SLAB/lockdep). 'Branch condition evaluates to a garbage value' at line 36 ('int* cache = kmalloc_caches[i]'). 'kmalloc_caches' is declared inside '#ifndef CONFIG_SLOB' (line 25-27) but used inside '#ifdef CONFIG_LOCKDEP' at line 36 (// (4) ERROR). When CONFIG_SLOB=true, 'kmalloc_caches' is not declared; in the desugared form it is hoisted but uninitialized, making 'cache = kmalloc_caches[i]' garbage, and then 'if(!cache)' at line 38 evaluates a garbage branch condition. This is the known vbdb bug. UNDER-CONSTRAINED: the presence condition '(CONFIG_SLOB AND NOT CONFIG_FORCE_MAX_ZONEORDER) OR (NOT CONFIG_SLOB AND NOT CONFIG_FORCE_MAX_ZONEORDER)' simplifies to 'NOT CONFIG_FORCE_MAX_ZONEORDER', which covers both CONFIG_SLOB=true (where the bug exists) and CONFIG_SLOB=false (where 'kmalloc_caches' IS declared and initialized, so no bug). The correct condition should be CONFIG_SLOB=true AND CONFIG_LOCKDEP=true. CONFIG_LOCKDEP is also missing — the function init_node_lock_keys() is only compiled under '#ifdef CONFIG_LOCKDEP'.
